plan.planning_summary: This study tests three distinct strategy axes for dual-band anti-reflection coating design on silicon: (1) a periodic quarter-wave reference stack to establish baseline performance, (2) a broadband-optimized stack treating both bands as one continuous range, and (3) a dual-band weighted optimization that explicitly trades performance between O-band and C-band. These axes are genuinely different because they optimize different objective functions over the same material system. Literature L04 motivates dual-band AR coating design, L12 and L18 support optimization algorithms for multilayer AR coatings, and L24 provides global optimization context. The substrate is silicon (si), incident medium is air, materials are ta2o5 (high index) and sio2 (low index). All routes respect the 12-layer maximum and 20-400 nm thickness constraints.

routes.title: Broadband Continuous Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Treating both wavelength bands as one continuous 1260-1565 nm range and optimizing layer thicknesses without band weighting will achieve lower overall average reflectance but may create performance imbalance between the two bands.
routes.design_principle: Broadband AR coatings use multiple layers with varying optical thicknesses to create multiple interference minima across a wide spectral range; optimizing over the full continuous span allows the solver to find thickness combinations that minimize integrated reflectance.

routes.title: Dual-Band Weighted Trade-Off Optimization

routes.design_principle: Dual-band AR coatings require thickness combinations that create interference minima at two distinct wavelength ranges; equal weighting forces the optimizer to find solutions that do not sacrifice one band for the other, exposing the Pareto frontier of the design space.
